title: Policy Lifecycle
summary: Policy lifecycle management covers the end-to-end handling of a policy—from quote, underwriting, issuance, endorsements, and billing to renewals, cancellations, reinstatements, and post-issue servicing—driving profitability through accurate pricing, efficient administration, controlled change management, and regulatory compliance via complete audit trails and data integrity. Policy origination begins with application intake, applies risk-rule-based underwriting to determine eligibility and pricing, and on approval issues a policy with calculated premiums, document delivery, and registration in the policy administration system to activate the lifecycle. Policy termination encompasses voluntary cancellations, insurer-initiated non-renewals or cancellations for cause, lapses, or misrepresentation/fraud, with defined refunds, notices to the insured and lienholders, and archiving of termination actions to satisfy retention and audit requirements.

guidance_context.sub_topic_description: Covers onboarding journey and underwriting fraud prevention.
guidance_context.parent_topic_description: Policy Lifecycle covers underwriting, issuance, amendments, and termination processes.

title: Policy Management
summary: Mid-term changes permit amendments to coverage, endorsements, or payment methods without a policy renewal, triggering risk re-rating and issuance of a revised premium statement; endorsements are captured as formal addenda to the policy record, creating an auditable trail of changes. title: Risk Management
summary: Fraud risk management provides governance-level oversight with monthly fraud-loss and recovery reporting to the board and senior management, complemented by real-time dashboards that monitor patterns by claim type, geography, and channel for timely mitigation. It combines proactive controls across the policy and claims lifecycle—underwriting data verification against authoritative sources and tailored investigations for opportunistic, organized, and internal fraud—with a blended rules-based and machine-learning risk-scoring model, governed by quarterly reviews and ongoing monitoring to ensure accuracy and regulatory alignment.

Recognizing opportunistic, organized, and internal fraud, the program monitors indicators such as inconsistent narratives and misrepresented information and applies tailored detection and investigation strategies accordingly.
